messages:
samir: Heads up — sales flagged a large enterprise (NovaHealth) asking for a hybrid pricing model: per-unit for baseline usage + bundled reserved credits for spikes. They want guidance on what we can offer and how it maps to our billing/console.
leah: They asked for something simple they can show legal: predictable monthly cost + burst. Their initial ask: 6B tokens/mo estimate, mostly chat+embeddings, PHI concerns so private deploy later. Want ~20% discount vs list for committed portion.
miguel: Do we have any analogs? Any customers with similar shape? Need token breakdown (chat vs embeddings vs rerank) and burst frequency.
anya: Support note — whatever we do we need clear UI/notifications: reserved balance, forecast, and an explicit overage policy. Customers always confuse "credits" vs "reserved capacity".
rahul: Finance: the discount asked (~20%) is material. We need a clear revenue model and guardrails (min commit, no indefinite rollover unless negotiated). Also need churn / usage risk sensitivity.
samir: Proposed options to evaluate quickly:
  A) Pure per-token volume tiers (simple, low implementation risk).
  B) Reserved-credit bundle: customer prepays X credits at discounted rate; unused credits rollback rules.
  C) Hybrid "commit + burst": monthly commit with cheaper committed unit, automatic pay-as-you-go overage at a higher unit price; optional cushion.
  Quick pros/cons: A = easy to sell but less predictable for customer. B = predictable revenue but requires billing + UI work and legal. C = most flexible but adds complexity to metering and fallback routing.
leah: Sales preference is C if we can make the business terms predictable. They want an explicit example they can include in an LOI.
miguel: I'll pull usage hist for top 5 similar customers and give token distribution + tail percentiles. Can do by EOD tomorrow.
anya: UX ask: show committed vs used, projected burn rate, and a switch for auto-burn vs manual approval for bursts. Also automated alerts at 70/90/100% of commit.
rahul: Finance guardrails to propose for product: min 6-month commit, max 3-month rollover for unused credits, built-in overage cap option (customer can opt into a hard cap to prevent bill shock).
samir: Acceptance criteria for product spec draft (PRD):
  - Clear definition of terms (committed token, reserved credit, overage price).
  - Billing behavior for partial month starts and early termination.
  - Console UX mocks for reserved balance + forecast.
  - Metering events and logs for audits.
  - Quickfall (fallback) behavior: if reserved pool exhausted, route to fallback model or deny.
  - Implementation risk estimate and minimal viable rollout plan (hosted API first).
leah: Also include negotiation playbook: what discount bands for 6/12/24 month commits, when to escalate to RevOps.
miguel: Adding: we should compute three scenarios (low/expected/high) of delta to unit economics and ops cost. I'll attach numbers.
opsbot: Ticket created: PRD-3421 "Hybrid commit + burst pricing spec" assigned to @samir, watchers: @leah @miguel @anya @rahul
samir: I'll draft the PRD and a short decision memo. Action items: @miguel fetch usage samples, @rahul provide unacceptable discount floor, @anya draft support runbook bullets, @leah confirm customer willingness to a 6-month min.
leah: Will confirm with customer this afternoon and update here. :thumbsup:
samir: Great — aim to have PRD first draft in 48 hours. TL;DR: sales wants hybrid; product needs data + finance guardrails + UX + implementation risk.
